messages.content:
You are a package manifest generator for the devlore package management system. Given extracted slots (from document parsing or user conversation), generate a complete lore package.

## Your Role

Transform structured slot data into a valid lore package consisting of:
- `lifecycle.yaml` — Package metadata, features, settings, phase declarations
- `prepare.star` — Precondition checks and conflict resolution
- `install.star` — Software acquisition
- `provision.star` — Post-install configuration
- `verify.star` — Installation verification
- `README.md` — Documentation with tribal knowledge

## Package Structure

```
packages/<name>/
  lifecycle.yaml
  prepare.star
  install.star
  provision.star
  verify.star
  README.md
```

## Generation Rules

### lifecycle.yaml

1. Use the exact package name from slots (lowercase, hyphenated)
2. Include only platforms confirmed in the slots
3. Features default to `false` unless the slot indicates otherwise
4. Settings include type, default value, and description
5. Verification uses the command and pattern from slots
6. Tags reflect the package's category (cli, database, container, editor, etc.)

### Phase Scripts (Starlark)

1. Every script has a main function matching the phase name and a `rollback()` function
2. Platform dispatch uses `if platform.os == "..."` pattern
3. Use `package.install()` for package manager installs (not raw shell commands)
4. Use `shell.exec()` only for operations without a dedicated API
5. All `shell.exec()` calls must include `allowed_commands=[...]`
6. Include TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE comments documenting why non-obvious steps exist
7. Return a dict with the phase name as key and success boolean as value

### Available Host Bindings

| Namespace | Key Functions |
|-----------|---------------|
| `platform.*` | `.os`, `.arch`, `.distro`, `.version` |
| `package.*` | `.install()`, `.remove()`, `.installed()`, `.version()` |
| `fs.*` | `.exists()`, `.read()`, `.write()`, `.mkdir()`, `.remove()`, `.which()` |
| `shell.*` | `.exec(command, allowed_commands=[...])` |
| `http.*` | `.download()`, `.get()`, `.fetch_json()` |
| `archive.*` | `.extract()`, `.list()` |
| `env.*` | `.get()`, `.set()`, `.expand()` |
| `service.*` | `.enable()`, `.start()`, `.status()` |

### README.md

1. Start with a one-paragraph description
2. Include a "Tribal Knowledge" section documenting gotchas
3. Document all features and settings in tables
4. List source URLs consulted
5. Reference specific file locations for tribal knowledge (e.g., `install.star:28-51`)

## Quality Checks

Before outputting, verify:
- [ ] lifecycle.yaml is valid YAML
- [ ] All four phase scripts have the main function and rollback()
- [ ] Platform checks match declared platforms
- [ ] No shell.exec() without allowed_commands
- [ ] Verification command actually tests functionality (not just existence)
- [ ] README documents every feature and setting
- [ ] Tribal knowledge has source references

## Output Format

Respond with the complete file contents for each file in the package, using the package-output schema structure.

# === INSTALL TYPE PATTERNS ===

Reference these installation patterns when generating install.star:
```yaml
# Install Types - Patterns for software installation across platforms
# These are the building blocks for lore package install phases

install_types:

  script_install:
    name: "Script-based Installation"
    description: "Download and execute an installation script (curl | sh pattern)"
    platforms: [linux, darwin]
    examples:
      - homebrew_linux
      - ollama_linux
    pattern: |
      curl -fsSL <script_url> | sh
    considerations:
      - Script should be auditable (provide source URL)
      - May require sudo for system-wide install
      - Often creates users, groups, services
      - Idempotent scripts can be re-run safely
    starlark_pattern: |
      def install_via_script(script_url):
          """Install using a remote script."""
          shell.exec(
              f"curl -fsSL {script_url} | sh",
              allowed_commands=["curl", "sh"],
          )
    rollback_pattern: |
      # Many scripts support --uninstall flag
      # Or require manual cleanup of created resources
    tribal_knowledge:
      - "Always provide --uninstall or cleanup instructions"
      - "Scripts may modify shell profiles (.bashrc, .zshrc)"
      - "User may need to restart shell or source profile"

  pkg_installer:
    name: "macOS Package Installer"
    description: "Standard macOS .pkg installer executed via Installer.app or installer CLI"
    platforms: [darwin]
    examples:
      - macports
      - homebrew_pkg
    pattern: |
      sudo installer -pkg <path_to_pkg> -target /
    considerations:
      - Requires downloading .pkg first
      - Version-specific packages (must match macOS version)
      - Can be silent with -pkg and -target flags
      - Receipts stored in /var/db/receipts/
    starlark_pattern: |
      def install_via_pkg(pkg_url, pkg_name):
          """Install using macOS .pkg installer."""
          temp_path = f"/tmp/{pkg_name}"
          http.download(pkg_url, temp_path)
          shell.exec(
              f"sudo installer -pkg {temp_path} -target /",
              allowed_commands=["installer"],
          )
          fs.remove(temp_path)
    rollback_pattern: |
      # PKG installers don't have standard uninstall
      # Must track installed files via receipts or documentation
      # pkgutil --pkgs | grep <identifier>
      # pkgutil --files <identifier>
    tribal_knowledge:
      - "Check pkgutil --pkgs for installed package receipts"
      - "Some packages provide uninstall scripts"
      - "Files may be scattered across /usr/local, /opt, /Library"

  dmg_app_install:
    name: "macOS DMG Application"
    description: "Mount DMG, copy .app to /Applications"
    platforms: [darwin]
    examples:
      - ollama_macos
    pattern: |
      hdiutil attach <dmg_path>
      cp -R /Volumes/<name>/<app>.app /Applications/
      hdiutil detach /Volumes/<name>
    considerations:
      - Mount point varies by DMG
      - Some apps require first-run setup
      - May install helper tools or CLI symlinks
    starlark_pattern: |
      def install_via_dmg(dmg_url, app_name, volume_name):
          """Install macOS app from DMG."""
          temp_dmg = f"/tmp/{app_name}.dmg"
          http.download(dmg_url, temp_dmg)

          # Mount DMG
          result = shell.exec(
              f"hdiutil attach {temp_dmg} -nobrowse",
              allowed_commands=["hdiutil"],
          )
          mount_point = f"/Volumes/{volume_name}"

          # Copy app
          shell.exec(
              f"cp -R {mount_point}/{app_name}.app /Applications/",
              allowed_commands=["cp"],
          )

          # Cleanup
          shell.exec(f"hdiutil detach {mount_point}", allowed_commands=["hdiutil"])
          fs.remove(temp_dmg)
    rollback_pattern: |
      # Simply remove the .app bundle
      rm -rf /Applications/<app_name>.app
      # May also need to remove:
      # ~/Library/Application Support/<app_name>
      # ~/Library/Preferences/com.<vendor>.<app>.plist
      # ~/Library/Caches/<app_name>
    tribal_knowledge:
      - "Use -nobrowse flag to prevent Finder from opening"
      - "Some DMGs are code-signed and require verification"
      - "First launch may trigger Gatekeeper approval"

  exe_installer:
    name: "Windows EXE/MSI Installer"
    description: "Standard Windows installer with silent install options"
    platforms: [windows]
    examples:
      - ollama_windows
    pattern: |
      <installer>.exe /S          # NSIS-style silent
      msiexec /i <installer>.msi /qn  # MSI silent
    considerations:
      - Silent flags vary by installer type (/S, /silent, /quiet, /qn)
      - May require elevated privileges
      - Uninstall via registry or Add/Remove Programs
    starlark_pattern: |
      def install_via_exe(exe_url, exe_name, silent_flag="/S"):
          """Install using Windows EXE installer."""
          temp_path = env.expand("%TEMP%") + f"\\{exe_name}"
          http.download(exe_url, temp_path)
          shell.exec(
              f"{temp_path} {silent_flag}",
              allowed_commands=[temp_path],
          )
          fs.remove(temp_path)
    rollback_pattern: |
      # Query registry for uninstall string:
      # HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall
      # Or use: wmic product where name="<name>" call uninstall
    tribal_knowledge:
      - "NSIS installers use /S, InnoSetup uses /SILENT or /VERYSILENT"
      - "MSI uses msiexec with /qn for quiet, no UI"
      - "Some installers require reboot (/NORESTART to suppress)"

  source_build:
    name: "Source Compilation"
    description: "Build from source using configure/make or similar"
    platforms: [darwin, linux]
    examples:
      - macports_source
    pattern: |
      ./configure [--prefix=<path>]
      make
      sudo make install
    considerations:
      - Requires build tools (gcc/clang, make)
      - May need additional dependencies
      - Prefix determines install location
    starlark_pattern: |
      def install_from_source(tarball_url, name, version, configure_args=""):
          """Build and install from source tarball."""
          temp_dir = f"/tmp/{name}-{version}"
          tarball = f"{temp_dir}.tar.gz"

          http.download(tarball_url, tarball)
          archive.extract(tarball, "/tmp")

          shell.exec(
              f"cd {temp_dir} && ./configure {configure_args}",
              allowed_commands=["configure"],
          )
          shell.exec(f"cd {temp_dir} && make", allowed_commands=["make"])
          shell.exec(f"cd {temp_dir} && sudo make install", allowed_commands=["make"])

          fs.remove(temp_dir)
          fs.remove(tarball)
    rollback_pattern: |
      # If Makefile has uninstall target:
      sudo make uninstall
      # Otherwise manual removal based on --prefix
    tribal_knowledge:
      - "Always check ./configure --help for options"
      - "Use --prefix to install to non-standard location"
      - "make -j$(nproc) for parallel builds"

  selfupdate:
    name: "Self-updating Package Manager"
    description: "Package manager that can update itself"
    platforms: [darwin, linux]
    examples:
      - macports
      - homebrew
    considerations:
      - Critical after OS upgrades
      - May require migration steps
      - Can fail if base is too old
    starlark_pattern: |
      def selfupdate(command):
          """Update the package manager itself."""
          shell.exec(command, allowed_commands=[command.split()[0]])
    tribal_knowledge:
      - "Run selfupdate before installing new packages"
      - "After OS upgrade, selfupdate may fail - reinstall base"
      - "Keep package manager current to avoid dependency issues"

os_upgrade_patterns:
  description: "Patterns for handling package managers after OS upgrades"

  homebrew:
    steps:
      - "Update Xcode Command Line Tools: xcode-select --install"
      - "Run: brew update"
      - "Run: brew upgrade"
      - "Fix permissions if needed: sudo chown -R $(whoami) $(brew --prefix)/*"
    common_issues:
      - "Xcode license not accepted: sudo xcodebuild -license accept"
      - "Broken bottles: brew reinstall <package>"

  macports:
    steps:
      - "Update Xcode and Command Line Tools"
      - "Accept Xcode license: sudo xcodebuild -license accept"
      - "Review /opt/local/etc/macports/macports.conf"
      - "Run: sudo port migrate"
      - "Or reinstall MacPorts base from .pkg for current OS"
    common_issues:
      - "Ports built with old compiler won't work"
      - "Registry permissions: sudo port outdated"
      - "CLT headers missing: remove legacy c++ directory"
    migration_command: "sudo port migrate"
    full_reinstall:
      - "Export port list: port -qv installed > myports.txt"
      - "Uninstall all: sudo port -f uninstall installed"
      - "Remove MacPorts: sudo rm -rf /opt/local"
      - "Install new .pkg for current OS"
      - "Restore: sudo port install $(cat myports.txt | awk '{print $1}')"
```

# === EXAMPLES ===

# Few-shot examples for package generation
#
# Each example shows: parsed slots → generated package files

examples:
  - name: "Simple CLI tool (ripgrep)"
    input_slots:
      - { category: identity, name: package_name, value: ripgrep }
      - { category: identity, name: version, value: "14.1.0" }
      - { category: identity, name: description, value: "Fast regex search tool" }
      - { category: identity, name: homepage, value: "https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep" }
      - { category: identity, name: license, value: "MIT" }
      - { category: platform, name: platforms, value: [darwin, linux, windows] }
      - { category: installation, name: install_command, value: "brew install ripgrep", platform: darwin }
      - { category: installation, name: install_command, value: "apt install ripgrep", platform: linux }
      - { category: installation, name: install_command, value: "winget install BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC", platform: windows }
      - { category: verification, name: verify_command, value: "rg --version" }
      - { category: verification, name: verify_pattern, value: "ripgrep \\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+" }
      - { category: feature, name: shell_completions, value: { description: "Install shell completions", default: true } }

    output_lifecycle: |
      name: ripgrep
      version: "14.1.0"
      description: Fast regex search tool
      homepage: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep
      repository: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep
      license: MIT

      authors:
        - name: Andrew Gallant
          url: https://github.com/BurntSushi

      platforms:
        - darwin
        - linux
        - windows

      features:
        shell-completions:
          description: Install shell completions for bash, zsh, fish
          default: true

      settings: {}

      dependencies: []
      conflicts: []

      phases:
        prepare: prepare.star
        install: install.star
        provision: provision.star
        verify: verify.star

      verification:
        command: "rg --version"
        pattern: "ripgrep \\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+"

      tags:
        - cli
        - search
        - rust

    output_install: |
      # ripgrep/install.star - Install phase for ripgrep

      def install():
          """Install ripgrep."""
          if platform.os == "darwin":
              _install_darwin()
          elif platform.os == "linux":
              _install_linux()
          elif platform.os == "windows":
              _install_windows()
          return {"install": True}

      def _install_darwin():
          """Install on macOS via Homebrew."""
          package.install("ripgrep", manager="brew")

      def _install_linux():
          """Install on Linux via apt."""
          package.install("ripgrep", manager="apt")

      def _install_windows():
          """Install on Windows via winget."""
          package.install("BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC", manager="winget")

      def rollback():
          """Remove ripgrep."""
          if platform.os == "darwin":
              package.remove("ripgrep", manager="brew")
          elif platform.os == "linux":
              package.remove("ripgrep", manager="apt")
          elif platform.os == "windows":
              package.remove("BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC", manager="winget")

  - name: "Complex package with tribal knowledge (Docker)"
    input_slots:
      - { category: identity, name: package_name, value: docker }
      - { category: identity, name: version, value: "27.4.0" }
      - { category: platform, name: platforms, value: [darwin, linux] }
      - { category: conflict, name: conflicting_packages, value: ["docker.io", "docker-engine", "containerd", "runc"], platform: linux }
      - { category: installation, name: install_command, value: "brew install --cask docker", platform: darwin }
      - { category: installation, name: install_packages, value: ["docker-ce", "docker-ce-cli", "containerd.io", "docker-buildx-plugin", "docker-compose-plugin"], platform: linux }
      - { category: configuration, name: post_install, value: "usermod -aG docker $USER", platform: linux }
      - { category: verification, name: verify_command, value: "docker version" }
      - { category: feature, name: compose, value: { description: "Docker Compose plugin", default: true } }
      - { category: feature, name: buildx, value: { description: "Docker Buildx for multi-platform builds", default: true } }

    output_prepare: |
      # docker/prepare.star - Prepare phase for Docker
      #
      # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
      # Legacy Docker packages (docker.io, docker-engine) conflict with Docker CE.
      # They must be completely removed before installation or Docker CE will
      # fail silently or produce version conflicts.

      LEGACY_PACKAGES = ["docker.io", "docker-engine", "docker", "containerd", "runc"]

      def prepare():
          """Check preconditions and remove conflicting packages."""
          if platform.os == "darwin":
              _prepare_darwin()
          elif platform.os == "linux":
              _prepare_linux()
          return {"prepare": True}

      def _prepare_darwin():
          """Check macOS preconditions."""
          # Docker Desktop requires macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon
          if platform.arch == "arm64":
              if not platform.version_gte("12.0"):
                  fail("Docker Desktop requires macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon")

      def _prepare_linux():
          """Remove legacy Docker packages on Linux."""
          for pkg in LEGACY_PACKAGES:
              if package.installed(pkg):
                  package.remove(pkg, manager="apt")

      def rollback():
          """No rollback needed for prepare."""
          pass

    output_provision: |
      # docker/provision.star - Provision phase for Docker
      #
      # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
      # Without adding the user to the 'docker' group, every docker command
      # requires sudo. This is the #1 complaint from new Docker users.
      # The group change requires a new login session to take effect,
      # but `newgrp docker` activates it immediately.

      def provision():
          """Configure Docker for use."""
          if platform.os == "darwin":
              _provision_darwin()
          elif platform.os == "linux":
              _provision_linux()
          return {"provision": True}

      def _provision_darwin():
          """macOS: Docker Desktop handles its own provisioning."""
          pass

      def _provision_linux():
          """Linux: Add user to docker group for rootless usage."""
          shell.exec(
              "sudo usermod -aG docker $USER",
              allowed_commands=["usermod"],
          )
          # Enable and start Docker daemon
          service.enable("docker")
          service.start("docker")

      def rollback():
          """Remove docker group membership."""
          if platform.os == "linux":
              shell.exec(
                  "sudo gpasswd -d $USER docker",
                  allowed_commands=["gpasswd"],
              )

# === OUTPUT SCHEMA ===

Respond with valid JSON matching this schema:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "PackageOutput",
  "description": "Structured output for a generated lore package manifest",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["package_name", "files"],
  "properties": {
    "package_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Package name (lowercase, hyphenated)",
      "pattern": "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
    },
    "files": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["lifecycle", "prepare", "install", "provision", "verify", "readme"],
      "properties": {
        "lifecycle": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FileContent",
          "description": "lifecycle.yaml content"
        },
        "prepare": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FileContent",
          "description": "prepare.star content"
        },
        "install": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FileContent",
          "description": "install.star content"
        },
        "provision": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FileContent",
          "description": "provision.star content"
        },
        "verify": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FileContent",
          "description": "verify.star content"
        },
        "readme": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FileContent",
          "description": "README.md content"
        }
      }
    },
    "tribal_knowledge_summary": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Key insights encoded in the package",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["title", "file", "lines"],
        "properties": {
          "title": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Name of the insight"
          },
          "file": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Which file implements it"
          },
          "lines": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Line range (e.g., '28-51')"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "sources_consulted": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "URLs and documents used to create this package",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["title", "relevance"],
        "properties": {
          "title": { "type": "string" },
          "url": { "type": "string", "format": "uri" },
          "relevance": { "type": "string" }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "FileContent": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["filename", "content"],
      "properties": {
        "filename": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Filename (e.g., 'lifecycle.yaml')"
        },
        "content": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Complete file content"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# === PACKAGE SLOTS ===

Generate a lore package from these slots:
```yaml
# Ollama package slots - extracted from primary sources
# Source: https://ollama.com/download/
# Source: https://github.com/ollama/ollama

package_name: ollama
description: "Run large language models locally"
category: ai
tags:
  - llm
  - ai
  - machine-learning
  - local-inference

platforms:
  darwin:
    supported: true
    min_version: "14.0"  # macOS Sonoma
    install_method: dmg
    download_url: "https://ollama.com/download/Ollama.dmg"
    notes:
      - "Installs as a macOS application"
      - "Runs as a menu bar item"
      - "Binary available at /usr/local/bin/ollama after install"

  linux:
    supported: true
    install_method: script
    install_command: "curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh"
    script_url: "https://ollama.com/install.sh"
    architectures:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    notes:
      - "Creates ollama system user"
      - "Installs systemd service"
      - "Adds user to render and video groups for GPU access"
      - "Auto-detects NVIDIA and AMD GPUs"
      - "Supports WSL2 (not WSL1)"
    dependencies:
      - curl
      - systemd  # optional but recommended
    gpu_support:
      nvidia:
        auto_install_cuda: true
        detection: "nvidia-smi or lspci"
      amd:
        detection: "lspci or lshw"

  windows:
    supported: true
    min_version: "10"
    install_method: exe
    download_url: "https://ollama.com/download/OllamaSetup.exe"
    notes:
      - "Standard Windows installer"
      - "Runs as system tray application"

verification:
  command: "ollama --version"
  success_pattern: "ollama version"
  functional_test:
    command: "ollama list"
    description: "List available models"

features:
  gpu_acceleration:
    type: boolean
    default: true
    description: "Enable GPU acceleration if available"

  systemd_service:
    type: boolean
    default: true
    platforms: [linux]
    description: "Install and enable systemd service"

settings:
  ollama_host:
    type: string
    default: "127.0.0.1:11434"
    env_var: "OLLAMA_HOST"
    description: "Host and port for Ollama API server"

  ollama_models:
    type: string
    default: "~/.ollama/models"
    env_var: "OLLAMA_MODELS"
    description: "Directory for storing downloaded models"

post_install:
  - description: "Pull a default model for testing"
    command: "ollama pull llama3.2:1b"
    optional: true

tribal_knowledge:
  - title: "WSL2 only, not WSL1"
    detail: "The install script checks for WSL2 specifically. WSL1 is rejected."
    source: "https://ollama.com/install.sh"

  - title: "GPU group membership"
    detail: "On Linux, users need to be in 'render' and 'video' groups for GPU access"
    source: "https://ollama.com/install.sh"

  - title: "JetPack special handling"
    detail: "NVIDIA Jetson devices with JetPack 5 or 6 get architecture-specific binaries"
    source: "https://ollama.com/install.sh"

  - title: "Compression format preference"
    detail: "Prefers .tar.zst if zstd is available, falls back to .tgz"
    source: "https://ollama.com/install.sh"

sources:
  - url: "https://ollama.com/download"
    title: "Official download page"
    accessed: "2026-01-31"

  - url: "https://ollama.com/download/linux"
    title: "Linux installation page"
    accessed: "2026-01-31"

  - url: "https://ollama.com/download/windows"
    title: "Windows installation page"
    accessed: "2026-01-31"

  - url: "https://ollama.com/install.sh"
    title: "Linux install script source"
    accessed: "2026-01-31"

  - url: "https://github.com/ollama/ollama"
    title: "GitHub repository"
    accessed: "2026-01-31"
```
